title: flow-control conservator: late-queue guard and soft-timeout amplification for continuous batching
author: Ivy Navarro
description: Motivation: in low-latency continuous-batching workloads we observed tail regressions when late-arriving KV-heavy requests starved smaller fast requests. This PR introduces the "flow-control conservator", a set of complementary scheduler heuristics to reduce starvation and stabilize p99 without sacrificing throughput. Key ideas: 1) late-queue guard: detect request cohorts that arrive near batch deadlines and limit their ability to evict ready slots unless they improve aggregate utilization; 2) soft-timeout amplification: when a request nears a soft timeout we accelerate slot admission and reduce coalescing for that cohort to preserve application-level SLOs; 3) aging score rebalance: incorporate an age/tokens composite score so small, latency-sensitive requests gain admission priority over long, KV-locked requests after a bounded wait; 4) KV-pin backoff: when a request holds a pinned KV cache entry and has already consumed multiple slots across retries, apply a probabilistic backoff to avoid repeated preemption of other work; 5) telemetry hooks and canary gating: new counters and traces allow gradual rollout and automatic rollback if throughput or e2e latency regress. Implementation summary: modified scheduler admission path to compute a conservative admission delta for late cohort members; added a soft-timeout fast-path that bypasses batching heuristics for at-most-N tokens when amplification conditions are met; added a token-aware age weight to the fairscore function; introduced a KV pin lease counter persisted on work descriptors and used by the admission filter to apply exponential backoff; wired feature flags and console metrics for rollout. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4821) updated - [x] unit tests for admission filter - [x] bench harness updated with KV-heavy and mixed profiles - [x] telemetry + dashboard wiring - [x] canary gating config - [x] upgrade notes and feature flag default off on stable clusters Deployment plan: land behind feature flag, enable for canary pool, observe p95/p99 and throughput for 48h, widen to 30% then full rollout. Rollback: flip feature flag; automated canary monitor will close flag on regressions. Why this is different from previous changes: rather than changing batch sizes or global timeouts, flow-control conservator focuses on per-request admission decisions and KV-aware backoffs so we avoid global throughput oscillations while removing starvation hotspots. Bench results (local perf-lab): mixed KV/short workload at 256-concurrency: baseline p99=210ms, mean=24ms; with conservator p99=150ms, mean=26ms; throughput delta -1.8% (within noise). Safety: defaults disabled in production; added regression tests that run in CI; feature flag named runtime.flow_control_conservator. Related: touches scheduling, kv cache behaviour, and batching flow; referenced prior thread on queue fairness (ENG-3120).

review_comments: Marcus Chen: Nice direction. Two immediate asks: 1) can we avoid a potential oscillation when the soft-timeout fast-path repeatedly bypasses coalescing? Add a cooldown. 2) please spell out the safety/rollback steps in the PR body.
Ivy Navarro: Added a per-cohort cooldown and documented rollback steps in the description and deploy plan. Cooldown default 2s and gated via feature flag. Updated tests to cover cooldown behavior.

Lena Ortega: Please include a unit test that simulates repeated KV pin renewals to ensure backoff triggers. Also note that the metrics emit a new tag 'flow_control_cohort' which may have high cardinality; consider bucketing.
Ivy Navarro: Added the unit test and changed the tag to a low-cardinality bucketed tag (short|medium|long) as requested.
Ravi Malhotra: Bench numbers look promising. Request one more integration run at 4x concurrency to ensure no hidden tail. Also suggest an e2e smoke in canary.
Ivy Navarro: Queued the integration run and added canary smoke steps to the deployment plan.
